card.name: Word just before a parenthetical or qualifier
card.fires_on: Single words in drug-label sentences that come right before a clause, a negation, or a bracketed aside, such as 'other routes', 'should not be used', 'a longer period' and 'Do not disperse'.

modes.label: Noun before parenthesis
modes.description: A noun such as routes or period is followed by an opening bracket with examples or a caveat.
modes.example: administration of methylene blue by other<< routes>> (such as oral tablets or local tissue

modes.label: Verb in a restriction
modes.description: A verb of use or handling appears in a 'should not' or 'do not' instruction.
modes.example: The gluteal muscle should not be<< used>> as an injection site because of the risk

modes.label: Joining or opening word
modes.description: A small joining word follows a statement of what was not studied or measured.
modes.example: Entecavir has not been studied as a treatment for HIV infection<< and>> is not recommended for this use.
